# Agent inventory: goodvibes-agent to products/agent

Every tracked file of goodvibes-agent (1602 files, from `git -C ~/Projects/goodvibes-agent ls-files`), read in full, with its disposition and, for a JEV or HOIST file, its decision points. Nothing is dropped unless it is specific to WRFC (the old write, review, fix, check controller and its workstream/attempt-judging machinery) or QEMU (sandbox templates and runtime); every other DROP line the intent document states for this product is void, per the owner ruling of 2026-09-26. That ruling reaches further than the products/agent section's own explicit callout: the intent document's products/agent Config bullet also names two files, `ensure-daemon-config-migrated.ts` and `ensure-daemon-enabled-migrated.ts` (plus their test), DROP, but neither is WRFC- or QEMU-specific, so that line is void too and both PORT unchanged, as genuine one-time migration scripts with no guesswork. No file of this product is dropped: WRFC code is JEV in the contract runner, as in the engine inventory, so `src/test/runtime/conversation-continuation-contract.test.ts` (the WRFC-gated work-chain escalation) is re-expressed against contract escalations. `src/test/tools/repl.test.ts` tests the engine REPL tool's sandbox gating, which outlives the QEMU backend, so it ports (see its row). Every other WRFC-touching file in the repository, including the roughly 90 `src/input/agent-workspace-*.ts` editor files, the `src/tools/agent-delegation-tool.ts` / `agent-work-plan-tool.ts` / `agent-workspace-tool.ts` / `agent-review-packet-*.ts` family, and the many tests that construct a `WrfcController` stub or reference `wrfc`-named fields, is JEV: it carries over, submitting contract-runner verbs where it used to submit WRFC verbs, or serving as the seam a contract-runner rewrite plugs into. Sub-agents themselves (the capability of running child agents) are kept throughout; only the WRFC controller's review/fix loop and its attempt-judging state machine are retired.

Every check in every file is read, understood for what it actually decides, and its disposition chosen on that (owner ruling 2026-09-27). Each row names the checks its file makes (each list, set, regex, pattern table, cutoff, threshold, lookup, comparison or classification whose result decides what the code does next) with its line in the goodvibes-agent source, what it decides and how, and the choice made: a Jev reading (a named battery or pattern) when the check answers a question of meaning with a guess, or code with the concrete reason its answer is its own definition (for example it compares two ids for equality, adds two numbers, caps a buffer, or dispatches on a closed enum the program itself produced). A category label (deterministic, fixed, security-critical, not judged) is never the reason to keep a check as code, and a blanket conversion is never the reason to make one a Jev reading: security checks, boundary lists, taint, trust tiers, sanitizers, redaction and format detection get the same reading as everything else. Where an agent check's engine counterpart is already decided in docs/inventory/engine.md, the row cites that engine row. A file is JEV when any of its checks is chosen as a Jev reading and PORT when none is; a HOIST file moves into the engine and records its checks and choices for that move.

Two other patterns recur across many areas and are called out once here rather than in every section: first, several products/agent HOIST bullets name a Jev reading (route planner choice, learning-curator classification, model-comparison candidate selection, personal-ops lane classification, date-parts extraction for schedules) that in practice lives in one shared module (most often `src/tools/agent-route-planner-helpers.ts` or the `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk` engine package) rather than in every file that calls it; those calling/facade files are marked HOIST or JEV with a note pointing at the file that actually holds the heuristic, rather than inventing a duplicate decision point. Second, a number of test files exercise engine-owned modules (`Orchestrator`, `WrfcController`, the memory/session spine transports, the gate's policy and exec-posture checks) that merely happen to live under this product's `src/test/` tree; those are marked HOIST or JEV to match the engine subsystem they actually test, not PORT, since the code under test is not really this product's own.

## Entry, renderer and shared utils

This slice covers the agent's main entry point (composition root, CLI flags, version, provider auth route display), the full terminal renderer (theme, escapes, status glyphs, primitives, layout, progress, thinking, compositor, conversation surface, overlays, markdown, code blocks, tool calls, diffs, modals), `src/utils`, and the matching tests under `src/test/renderer` and `src/test/utils`.

Every file was re-read check by check (E.16) and each row names its checks, what each decides and the choice. Most checks here stay code for a stated reason: they dispatch on closed enums the program itself produced (tool call status, fleet node state, activity kind, theme mode), do width, scroll, luminance and duration arithmetic, or parse grammars a program or a standard defines (ANSI and OSC escapes, the program's own markdown and diff output). Seven files make a check that answers a question of meaning with a guess and are JEV: `agent-workspace.ts` (whether an editor message reports a blocking problem, agent.workspace.editor-message-blocking), `mcp-workspace.ts` (the tone of the MCP status line, agent.mcp.status-tone), `model-workspace.ts` (whether a provider serves models from local hardware, routing.catalog-provider-access), `system-message.ts` (error, warning or information, agent.renderer.system-message-severity), `tool-call.ts` (which argument names what a call acts on when no named field exists, agent.renderer.tool-key-arg), and the two tests that pin the model-workspace and system-message guesses.

Nothing here is specific to WRFC or QEMU, so nothing is dropped. The `wrfc` settings category in `settings-modal.ts` and `settings-modal-helpers.ts` is label and description text; it is renamed to contract runner terms along with the settings keys it describes.

## Core and config

## Core and config inventory: goodvibes-agent src/core and src/config to products/agent

Every file of this slice (`src/core`, `src/config`, and their matching tests under `src/test/core` and `src/test/config`, from `git -C ~/Projects/goodvibes-agent ls-files`), re-read check by check (E.16). The intent document's Config bullet under products/agent names `ensure-daemon-config-migrated.ts` and `ensure-daemon-enabled-migrated.ts` DROP, but neither is WRFC or QEMU specific, so per the owner ruling of 2026-09-26 that line is void and both port as one-time migrations. No file here is dropped.

Most checks in `src/config` and `src/core` stay code for a stated reason: exact lookup against keys and enums the program declares (setting ownership, secret tiers from the declared key list, money by the schema's `unit` mark), arithmetic (token counts, hardware fit ratios over byte counts), or formats a program writes (`/proc/meminfo`, `nvidia-smi` CSV, the compactor's handoff header). The JEV files: `settings-search-vocabulary.ts` (its alias words give way to one Jev rerank of the settings catalog for the person's query, agent.settings.catalog-rank), `conversation-rendering.ts` (the error-navigation stop takes the error answer of agent.renderer.system-message-severity), `hardware-profile.ts` (a model's parameter count, agent.core.model-size), `plain-language.ts` and `setup-incomplete-hint.ts` (whether copy uses internal vocabulary or command syntax, agent.copy.plain-language), `system-message-router.ts` (message priority through the engine's engine.runtime.system-message-priority), and the tests that pin them. `activity-feed.ts` and `system-message-noise.ts` stay code: the first maps the leading tag this program writes to an activity kind by an exact table, following the owner ruling in engine.md row `sdk/src/platform/runtime/system-message-policy.ts:25`, and the second matches fixed templates this program's own writers produce.

`src/test/core` holds ten tests of engine-owned modules (`Orchestrator`, `classifyIntent`, replay, lineage, session memory, compaction, tool-result reconciliation, `InfiniteBuffer`) imported from `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk` or `@pellux/goodvibes-terminal-shell`. They are HOIST with the engine code they test, and each row cites the engine.md row that decides that code's checks. `orchestrator.test.ts` builds a `wrfcController` stub in every test; that seam and its `wrfc:*` keys move to the contract runner's equivalents.

Files: 92. PORT 70, JEV 12, HOIST 10, DROP 0. Decision points: 7.

## Audio, shell, permissions, trust and verification

This slice covers `src/audio`, `src/shell`, `src/permissions`, `src/trust`, `src/capabilities`, `src/verification`, and the matching tests under `src/test/audio`, `src/test/voice`, `src/test/shell`, `src/test/permissions`, `src/test/trust`, `src/test/capabilities` and `src/test/verification`, every file re-read check by check (E.16).

Audio, capture and shell code decides by process exit codes, byte comparisons, thresholds the owner configures and closed enums, and stays code for those reasons. In permissions, `prompt.ts` is JEV (the risk level shown for a request that carries no analysis came from a fixed category ternary and now comes from the gate's stakes reading), while `approval-posture.ts` and `broker-approval.ts` mirror typed decisions and owner settings and are PORT; the permission tests are JEV where the gate behaviour they pin now reads through engine.gate.side-effect and engine.gate.risk-family (engine.md rows `sdk/src/platform/permissions/manager.ts` and `sdk/src/platform/gate/reading.ts`). In verification, `live-verifier.ts` (credential spans in release reports, agent.verification.release-redaction, and cross-space knowledge records, agent.knowledge.scope-contamination), `settings-consumed-keys.ts` (whether a file acts on a setting or only names it, agent.verification.setting-consumer), `verification-ledger-surfaces.ts` (whether a readiness statement establishes its dimension, agent.verification.readiness-dimension) and `verification-ledger.ts` (whether a command or surface needs a live external outcome, agent.verification.external-outcome) are JEV with their tests. Capabilities and trust move into the engine (HOIST); their rows record each check and its choice for E.15.

## CLI

Every file of this slice (`src/cli` and its matching tests under `src/test/cli`, plus `src/test/cli-flags.test.ts`), re-read check by check (E.16). The intent document's PORT bullet list for the agent's CLI names most of these modules, but that is not a ruling that a module makes no guess; each file was read on its own evidence.

`provider-classification.ts` (with its test) is HOIST to the engine's providers subsystem, its provider-id sets becoming routing.catalog-provider-access readings. The JEV files: `agent-knowledge-runtime.ts` (errors this file did not raise are read by engine.failure-reading; cross-space records by agent.knowledge.scope-contamination), `fleet-command.ts` (attempt judging is contract.best-of-n in the contract runner), `management.ts` (which provider serves a model id the catalog does not list, agent.cli.model-provider), `openclaw-import.ts` (memory class by engine.tools.memory-class; the Agent tool category of an OpenClaw tool name by agent.cli.openclaw-tool-category), `package-verification.ts` (doc claims, command mentions, readiness text and release notes, the agent.release batteries), `parser.ts` (which provider a slash-bearing model id names, routing.model-identity), `redaction.ts` (credential-bearing config paths outside the schema by config.credential-key, credential spans in text by engine.redaction.credential, as engine.md decided for the engine's redaction module), and the tests that pin them. `channel-profiles-command.ts` and `help.ts` are PORT: their checks are closed enums the command contracts define and fields of files the build writes. Code stays, with its reason in each row, for the owner's confirmation flags, the parser's own command tables, bind-port equality, status findings on owner settings, checksum comparison and date arithmetic.

For every other error (the browser agent SDK client calls, a failed `fetch`), Jev `engine.failure-reading` (the engine battery that already reads error text for its category and connection-failure facts), mapped onto the same closed failure kinds, as the agent-knowledge-runtime.ts file row chooses. |

| `src/cli/provider-classification.ts:L98-L101`, `SUBSCRIPTION_PROVIDERS`, `LOCAL_PROVIDERS`, `SELF_HOSTED_PROVIDERS`, `CLOUD_ACCOUNT_PROVIDERS` | Fixed provider-id sets decide whether a provider is sold as a subscription, runs locally, is an operator-run gateway, or needs cloud account credentials; unlisted providers fall through to the auth mode or `unknown`. | Jev `routing.catalog-provider-access` (local server? access sold as a plan?) plus new items for operator-run gateway and cloud account credentials, read once per provider from its published facts (the choice engine.md row `sdk/src/platform/providers/model-catalog-cache.ts` makes); hoisted with the module. |
| `src/cli/redaction.ts:L33`, `SENSITIVE_PATH_PATTERN` | A last-segment word list decides whether a config path holds a credential; it misses `cloudflare.*Ref` and the card fields and masks `keyFile`, a path. | Jev `config.credential-key` for paths outside the config schema, with schema keys answered by the declaration and undeclared schema keys read by the credential-scope check, as goodvibes-jev's terminal-shell cli-redaction.ts does. |
| `src/cli/redaction.ts:L103-L112`, `SECRET_LIKE_TEXT_PATTERNS` (`sk-`, `ghp_`, `gho_`, `ghu_`, `ghs_`, `github_pat_`, `xoxb`/`xapp`/`xoxp`/`xoxa` prefixes with length floors, and `name:secret@` without a scheme) | Vendor-prefix and length regexes decide which spans of text are credentials; other key formats pass and ordinary text of the same shape is masked. | Jev yes/no per token of the text, all tokens of a window in one request, engine.redaction.credential (the choice engine.md row `sdk/src/platform/utils/redaction.ts` and decision row `:8` make for the same patterns, issuer prefixes included). |
| `src/cli/redaction.ts:L174`, `redactText` keyword assignment forms | The word before `=` or `:` (`access_token`, `api_key`, `secret`, `password`, `token`) decides whether the following value is a credential, so `token: 4096` is masked. | Jev yes/no per candidate value, engine.redaction.credential: "is this value a credential?" |

Two further JEV files carry no decision-points row of their own, matching the webui inventory's precedent for WRFC-state views and for docs describing a JEV surface: `channel-profiles-command.ts` (the `--permission-mode` enum is a closed-set validation today; the judgment of which preset fits a given situation's stakes will live in the engine gate's Jev-scored stakes table, not in this CLI file) and `fleet-command.ts` (the best-of-N attempt judgment already lives in the orchestration engine's `proposeAttemptWinner`, outside this CLI file, which only renders the proposal and gates the confirm-required pick). `help.ts` documents both surfaces but performs no judgment of its own. `provider-classification.ts` (HOIST) is a deterministic fixed-set classification relocating to sit beside the engine's other provider-registry code; it does not become a Jev reading.

## Providers, types, and top-level (root, scripts, docs, release, packaging)

Every tracked file of goodvibes-agent under `src/providers`, `src/types`, `src/test/providers`, and every top-level file outside `src/`, re-read check by check (E.16). The provider registry, classification, fallback and health logic lives in `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk` (packages/engine in the new tree); this repo's `src/providers/reasoning-effort-surface.ts` and its tests consume that behaviour, and each row cites the engine.md row that decides it.

Docs, policy briefs and skills are prose with no checks and are PORT; where they name WRFC or describe a decision that becomes a Jev reading in its own module, the text is reworded when that module lands, as each row states. Three scripts make a check that answers a question of meaning with a guess and are JEV: `internal-identifier-rule.ts` (which spans of a line name an internal planning identifier, a Jev extraction per line as in tui.md and webui.md), `package-install-check.ts` (whether a launch transcript reports a failure, agent.release.launch-transcript) and `release.ts` (whether a release note line is a commit-log entry, agent.release.notes-quality item `commit_reference`). Nothing here is WRFC or QEMU specific; nothing is dropped.

Files: 94. PORT 91, JEV 3, HOIST 0, DROP 0. Decision points: 3.

| `scripts/internal-identifier-rule.ts:L53`, `INTERNAL_IDENTIFIER_PATTERNS` | Thirteen token-shape regexes, applied per line at L137-L145, guess whether a line of tracked text names an internal planning identifier (wave, work-order, debt-register, security finding, UX and lettered finding ids); the file's own header (L20-L44) records the shapes as a trade between false positives (function keys, control-character set names, Slack ids, IMAP tags, the W3C acronym) and misses | Jev extraction per line, fanned out in one request: which spans of this line name an internal planning or coordination identifier as `OWNER_DOCTRINE` (L49-L51) defines it; same question as tui.md `scripts/internal-identifier-rule.ts:43-62` |

## Runtime (bootstrap, composition, spine transports)

The alphabetical first half of `src/runtime` (through `tool-permission-safety.ts`, `client/*`, `store/*`, `diagnostics/panels/*`, `onboarding/*`) plus its matching tests under `src/test/runtime`, re-read check by check (E.16).

Most of it is the agent's composition root and the seams that reach the daemon: bootstrap phases, approvals, fleet and session frames, the runtime store, onboarding, update and archive handling. Those checks stay code for a stated reason: closed enums the broker or daemon writes, owner settings and confirmation flags, token presence, HTTP status codes, file mode bits, archive path grammar and version comparison. The checks that answer a question of meaning with a guess read through Jev: the execution ledger's route kind and argument previews (`execution-ledger.ts`, engine.gate.side-effect `kind` and engine.gate.ledger-arg), the permission category when the permission manager throws (`tool-permission-safety.ts`, engine.gate.side-effect `kind`), the agent's command obfuscation checks (`index.ts`, engine.gate.side-effect `obfuscated`), memory usage (`memory-usage-wiring.ts`, engine.state.memory-usage), the model that replaces an unresolvable configured model at boot (`provider-boot.ts`, agent.runtime.boot-model-replacement), sibling attempt judging (`services.ts`, contract.best-of-n in the contract runner), and the tests that pin the child failure reason and compaction quality readings. `execution-ledger.ts`, `tool-permission-safety.ts`, `agent-exec-posture.ts`, `agent-operator-policy.ts`, the spine transports and memory usage wiring move into the engine (HOIST) and record their checks and choices for E.15.

Files: 107. PORT 94, JEV 5, HOIST 8, DROP 0. Decision points: 8.

| File | Disposition | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `src/runtime/agent-browser.ts` | PORT | Binds the engine's surface-agnostic `BrowserEngine` and `BrowserSessionManager` to this product's answers: profile, screenshot and managed driver roots and driver search directories under the Agent surface root, the missing-host-script fix sentence, the untrusted-content port and the session-write ledger. Nothing here is WRFC or QEMU specific; nothing is dropped. Most files move into the engine (HOIST) and record each check and its choice for E.15.

The checks that answer a question of meaning with a guess: the registry searches over personas, routines, notes, documents, research runs, research sources and skills (a literal substring test, now the engine's rerank engine.tools.registry-rank), the settings catalog ranking (`harness-control.ts`, agent.settings.catalog-rank), credential detection in settings, receipts, local records and source URLs (config.credential-key, engine.redaction.credential and engine.tools.credential-value, as engine.md decided for the engine's redaction), string flags that mean yes or no (engine.tools.boolean-value), connected-host failure kinds in three copies of one keyword ladder (engine.failure-reading), per-turn memory relevance and its band (engine.state.memory-search), prompt tier guidance (routing.model-tier), research source credibility and its default score (agent.research.source-credibility), setup receipt status and step (agent.setup.receipt-status, agent.setup.receipt-step), duplicate skill drafts (agent.skills.draft-duplicate), and card details in outbound messages (the engine's card reading). ## Input: agent-workspace editors (contract-runner tools)

The intent document's DROP line for products/agent ("The delegation, agent orchestration, work plan, workspace action and editor runners, the workspace tool and the review packet tools") is void per the owner ruling of 2026-09-26: nothing is dropped unless it is specific to WRFC or QEMU. None of the `src/input/agent-workspace*.ts` editor and panel files or the 13 matching workspace tests is WRFC-controller or QEMU-sandbox code: they are in-modal form plumbing (field specs, confirm-gated slash-command strings, runtime-snapshot assembly, navigation, search, token routing) that dispatches to slash commands and tools owned elsewhere. The delegation and work-plan editors submit contract-runner verbs where they submitted WRFC verbs; the review-packet editors are document-review handoffs for human reviewers, not WRFC, and keep their targets.

Every file was read in full and each row names every check its file makes, with its line, what it decides and the choice made. Seven source files guess at meaning on their own and are JEV: `agent-workspace-channel-triage.ts` and `agent-workspace-research-report-editor.ts` (keyword regexes decide which spans of text or which URL query parameters are credentials to mask), `agent-workspace-settings.ts` (a keyword regex decides which config keys hold credentials; read through the engine's `holdsCredential`), `agent-workspace-context-snapshot.ts` (five substrings decide whether an MCP server gives browser or desktop control), `agent-workspace-search.ts` (literal word matching and hand-tuned field weights decide which actions match a search and which comes first), `agent-workspace-workplan-editor-submission.ts` (a synonym table decides which work plan status a typed word means) and `agent-workspace-delegation-editor-submission.ts` (its `review`/`wrfc` field requested the retired write-review-fix-confirm loop; every delegated contract is now judged by Jev with nudges to the sub-agent). Two tests change with them. Everything else compares ids, reads typed confirmations the form instructs, dispatches on editor kinds the program defines or does arithmetic, and is PORT; `agent-workspace-document-ops-editor.ts`, `agent-workspace-review-packet-snapshot.ts` and `agent-workspace-review-packet-utils.ts` change JEV to PORT on that reading (their freshness flags compare artifact ids and timestamps).

Files: 110. PORT 101, JEV 9, HOIST 0, DROP 0. Decision points: 10.

| Main `agent-workspace.ts` orchestrator | 1 | 1 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

## Input: commands, handler routes and other input modules

This fragment covers the first alphabetical half of `goodvibes-agent`'s `src/input` tree (101 files): the top-level input handler modules (`handler*.ts`, `feed-context-factory.ts`, `keybindings.ts`, `input-history.ts`, `search.ts`, `selection-modal.ts`, the model-picker family, the session/profile-picker modals, `mcp-workspace.ts`, `concealed-input.ts`/`plain-line-input.ts`, `file-picker.ts`, `command-registry.ts`, `autocomplete.ts`, `command-args-hint.ts`, `commands.ts`) plus the alphabetically-earlier half of `src/input/commands/*` (from `agent-local-library-args.ts` through `vibe-runtime.ts`). The roughly 90 agent-workspace files and their tests are a separate slice and are excluded here, per the intent document's Input bullet under products/agent.

Every file was read in full and each row names every check its file makes, with its line, what it decides and the choice made. Most of this half is command-surface plumbing over engine APIs: it parses arguments by the command's own grammar, calls a typed SDK client and prints a report. Six source files make a guess of their own and are JEV: `model-picker-types.ts` (a regex ladder guesses a model's vendor family, read through `engine.runtime.model-family` as tui.md and engine.md do), `file-picker.ts` (two fixed directory names decide what is dependency or build output, the reading tui.md records), `session-workflow.ts` (the session export's credential spans, read as engine.md's `utils/redaction.ts` row decides), `shell-core.ts` (the help category of a command missing from the built-in lists), `notify-runtime.ts` (which parts of a webhook URL may be shown) and `delegation-runtime.ts` (its `--review`/`--wrfc` flag switched the retired WRFC review on or off; every delegated unit is now judged by Jev in the contract runner). `command-registry.ts` changes JEV to PORT: its scorer completes a partly typed command name against the registered names, the same choice tui.md makes. No file here is specific to WRFC or QEMU, so there are no DROP rows.

Files: 101. PORT 95, JEV 6, HOIST 0, DROP 0. Decision points: 6.

The second alphabetical half of `src/input` (excluding the agent-workspace files, covered by the section above): 13 source modules directly under `src/input/` (the settings-modal family, the setup-wizard receipts aggregator, the shell-passthrough runner, the slash-command parser, and the submission-intent/router pair) plus the 88 test files under `src/test/input/` whose alphabetical range falls in this half. All 101 files were read in full and each row names every check its file makes, with its line, what it decides and the choice made. None is specific to WRFC or QEMU, so there are no DROP rows. The source modules make no guess of their own; the settings modal's `wrfc` category becomes the contract runner's `contract` category holding the `contract.*` settings (wrfc-to-jev.md).

Fifteen tests are JEV. Two make a guess in their own code: `command-aliases-lint.test.ts` (a verb list decides which commands are destructive) and `settings-modal-payments.test.ts` (a regex decides which config keys hold raw card material). The others pin behaviour whose check moves to a Jev reading and run against a judgment test double with fixed readings: the secret-looking content refusal exercised by `agent-skills-command.test.ts`, `personas-command.test.ts`, `routines-command.test.ts` and `vibe-command.test.ts` is a keyword-assignment guess at whether a value is a secret (carried by the `src/agent/memory-safety.ts` row, as engine.md's `utils/redaction.ts` row decides), and the recall, notify, channels, knowledge, session export, image input, model picker and delegation tests pin memory-search order and injection reasons, URL masking, credential spans, knowledge relevance, request routing, vendor family and contract-runner judging.

## Tools: harness (product tools over engine verbs)

This slice covers the `agent_harness` product tool family: the single giant mode-dispatch
tool (`agent-harness-tool.ts`), its schema/types/utils, and the roughly 90 supporting files
under `src/tools/` that each own one harness surface (autonomy, personal ops, learning
curator, model routing/readiness, memory, research, document ops, setup posture, workspace
actions/editors, remote peers, and more), plus the matching tests under `src/test/tools/`.
Architecturally almost everything here is a thin, deterministic dispatch/catalog layer that
calls down into engine verbs (`ToolRegistry`, `ProcessManager`, `ConfigManager`, work-plan and
artifact stores, etc.) that already live in the engine SDK; nothing in this slice needed to be
hoisted out to `packages/engine` on its own account. The decision-point density is real but
concentrated: it lives in the handful of files that turn free text or arbitrary metadata into a
typed judgment (model readiness/routing, learning-curator scoring, personal-ops lane
classification, autonomy intake/date-parts extraction, catalog/settings search relevance,
document reviewer readiness, execution-history/interactive-runtime classification). Everything
else is exact-match/case-insensitive/substring resolution chains, static catalogs, typed-field
dispatch, or deterministic security/redaction boundaries, and ports intact.

No file in this slice is WRFC-controller-specific or QEMU-sandbox-specific, including the four
`agent-harness-workspace-*-runner*.ts` / `agent-harness-workspace-editor-*.ts` files that the
original (voided) intent DROP bullet named. Read in full, they are generic action/editor
dispatch mechanics (typed `action.kind` / `editor.kind` switches, confirmation gating, tool-registry
handoffs) with no attempt-judging or sandbox logic in them, so per the owner's 2026-09-26 ruling
they PORT rather than DROP.

## Tools: other agent tools (route planner, policy, registries-facing tools)

This slice covers 91 files: all of them are test files under `src/test/tools/` (and `src/test/tools/shared/`) that were partitioned into this slice as the "tests" half of the products/agent tools inventory (the companion source-file slice, `tools-other-b`, covers the matching `src/tools/*.ts` files; the harness family, `agent-harness-*`, is a separate already-completed slice). Every disposition below is based on reading each test file in full and judging what it proves about the source module it exercises, the same way `docs/inventory/webui.md` disposes end-to-end and integration tests by what they pin rather than by file name alone. Two files here (`agent-route-tool.test.ts` and `agent.test.ts`) pin the two biggest decision points in the whole agent product: the route planner's keyword ladder, and the WRFC sub-agent orchestration controller.

Files: 91. PORT 40, JEV 30, HOIST 21, DROP 0.

| File | Disposition | Note |
|---|---|---|
| `src/test/tools/agent-accounts-tool.test.ts` | HOIST | Pins the accounts registry's deterministic security boundary (secret-value refusal, the untrusted-content-ledger check that blocks registering an account off content read this turn) and alias minting. Bucket member of the intent's "personal ops harness, Google and accounts tools" HOIST group; this test itself exercises only the deterministic trust boundary, not the lane-classification decision point named for that group. |

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-route-tool.ts` (tested by `agent-route-tool.test.ts`), the whole-file `route` planner | A hand-built keyword ladder over a large fixed catalog of route ids: free-text queries are matched word-by-word against per-route trigger phrases with a numeric relevance `score`, disambiguating e.g. "take a screenshot of the screen" (desktop) from "fill out the contact form... submit it" (browser), and "run claude code with pty=true and handle sudo prompts" (interactive-process-capability) from "write process documentation" (not that route) purely by wording overlap. | Hoisted in E.4 as the engine task route planner: `routing.task-route.pick`, a Choice over the route catalog plus one Noul fit question per route in one request, with the slots battery and the named-id selector in the same planning pass (packages/engine/sdk/src/platform/routing/task-routes/). |
| `agent-tool.ts` / `WrfcController` (from `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk/platform/agents`, tested by `agent.test.ts`) | The WRFC controller's write-review-fix-check loop and attempt judging: `reviewMode:"wrfc"` plus `template:"reviewer"` triggers ad hoc owner-chain role assignment (`wrfcRole:"owner"`, `wrfcRouteReason:"root-review-role-normalized"`) and collapses a multi-agent WRFC fan-out into one authoritative chain, tracked as free-standing state on each agent record rather than as judged, quantized work. | The contract runner: goal + acceptance criteria set once, decomposed into units/groups judged by Jev the moment each completes, with best-of-N as candidate selection instead of a WRFC review/revision state machine. Sub-agents are kept as the execution substrate (per the standing project ruling); only the WRFC-controller state machine and its owner-chain heuristics are retired. |
| `agent-tool-policy-guard.ts` (tested inside `agent.test.ts`) | A large, hand-maintained allow/deny list per tool name (exec limited to foreground/serial; read-only mode enumerations for remote/channel/mcp/fetch/state/control/analyze/registry/find/web_search/task/team/worklist/packet/query), each enforced by exact string/enum matching. | Named in intent as "The tool policy guard and every policy and posture tool, to the gate": HOIST. E.5 reading (2026-09-27 ruling): the mode enumerations stay code because they are the Agent product's declaration of which modes its main-conversation tools offer (a tool schema the product publishes, not a reading of any call's content); the checks inside that did judge content (secret paths for read, hazardous settings keys, the confirmation text) are Jev readings. |
| `agent-model-compare-tool.ts` (tested by `agent-model-compare-tool.test.ts`), `mode:"judge"` | A prompt-and-parse judge: the calling model reads two blind candidate outputs itself and reports a free-text `winnerBlindId` + `reasons` through the tool call, with no structured rubric or independent evaluation. | Intent's explicit "Model comparison judgment is JEV, with candidate selection replacing the prompt-and-parse judge": a Jev choice/rerank pattern over the two (or N) blinded candidates against the supplied rubric. |
| `agent-research-sources-tool.ts` (tested by `agent-research-sources-tool.test.ts`), `add`/`review` actions | `credibility` (`high`/`medium`/`low`) and a numeric `score` are supplied directly by the calling model as unstructured judgment on each captured source, with no evaluation step in between. | Intent's explicit "research-source credibility scored": a Jev score reading (rubric-scored credibility) replacing the model's free-typed value. |
| `agent-harness-operator-methods.ts`'s catalog search (tested by `operator-method-catalog-search.test.ts`) | A hand-tuned, multi-tier text matcher: exact phrase, then per-word AND across id/title/description, then a "relaxed" single-word fallback with a "near misses" note, plus an "ambiguous" branch when a plain word matches many methods, replacing an earlier, even cruder "one contiguous substring over a collapsed label" matcher that a real incident showed returned zero results for `query:"google"` against 434 methods. | A Jev existence-check/rerank pattern over the operator-method catalog (structured relevance reading) instead of a hand-tuned word-overlap ladder with ad hoc fallback tiers. |
| `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk` registry tool's `mode:"recommend"` (tested by `registry-tool.test.ts`) | "Sorts results by keyword relevance to task": ranks skills/agents/tools against a free-text `task` string by naive keyword/description overlap (e.g. ranking `code-review` above `test-driven` for "review code quality"). | Matches intent's engine "skills | Skill documents, progressive disclosure, CRUD | JEV: relevance by rerank": a Jev rerank pattern over the registry entries against the task description. |
| `agent-vibe-tool.ts`, `action:"import_persona"` (tested by `agent-vibe-tool.test.ts`) | An arbitrary, user-authored VIBE.md file's name/description/body is adopted directly into an active, reviewed persona on `confirm:true` + `explicitUserRequest` alone; no content screening step is visible before the persona becomes active. | Intent's explicit "The vibe file and vibe confirmation routes also carry over; they are screened by the engine policy checklist, which is a JEV use": a Jev policy-checklist pattern screening imported persona content before it can become active. |
| `agent-work-plan-tool.ts` / `agent-workspace-tool.ts` / `agent-delegation-tool.ts` / `agent-review-packet-presets-tool.ts` / `agent-review-packet-share-tool.ts` (the DROP-voided bucket) | Ad hoc dispatch of work items to sub-agents via freeform `agent { mode: "spawn" }` / `batch-spawn` calls with manually authored `successCriteria`/`context` strings, plus self-authored preset/receipt artifacts (freshness judged only by artifact `createdAt` comparison) standing in for structured, judged units of work. | Per the owner ruling of 2026-09-26 ("the DROP-voided delegation/work-plan/workspace/review-packet tools... become JEV onto the contract runner... NOT DROP"): these tools submit contract-runner verbs (units/groups/deliverables judged by Jev as they complete) instead of ad hoc `agent`-tool dispatch and self-authored presets. |

The second alphabetical half of `src/tools/*.ts` in goodvibes-agent, excluding the `agent-harness-*` family (a separate, already-completed slice). This batch is dominated by two things: a large family of thin routing facades that translate a small closed-set `action`/`mode` alias into a call on `agent_harness` (dispatch over a known vocabulary, not guesswork, so most stay PORT or HOIST depending on whether the underlying subsystem is agent-specific or platform-generic), and the route planner (`agent-route-planner*`), which is the single largest concentration of keyword-ladder guesswork in this slice and is explicitly named in the intent document as the JEV target for the route tool. The delegation/work-plan/workspace/vibe/review-packet tools are JEV per the owner ruling of 2026-09-26 (they submit contract-runner verbs, not DROP). 90 files: 21 PORT, 18 JEV, 51 HOIST, 0 DROP (the six route planner and route tool files were hoisted into engine routing in E.4).

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `agent-route-planner-helpers.ts` (dozens of functions, e.g. `scheduleLike` L25-43, `autonomousLike` L45-60, `mediaGenerationLike` L75-79, `browserControlLike` L81-110, `personalOpsLike` L289-315, `personalOpsLaneFromText` L317-326, `securityPermissionLike`/`securityStatusLike`/`securityFindingLike`/`securityPolicyExplainLike` L485-573, `channelSetupLike`/`channelTriageLike`/`channelDeliveriesLike` L382-396, `modelRouteReadinessLike` L467-483) | Hundreds of literal substring/`hasAny`/`hasAll` checks against a lowercased free-text user request, classifying it into a route category, lane, or effect posture | Hoisted in E.4: every predicate is replaced by the `routing.task-route.slots` yes/no and closed-vocabulary questions and the `routing.task-route.named-id` selector (task-routes/slots.ts, named-ids.ts). |
| `agent-route-planner.ts`, `buildCandidates`/`confidence` (L62-103) | Every keyword-matched candidate gets a hand-tuned integer score (35-100); candidates are sorted by score and the top one becomes "preferred" | Hoisted in E.4: the preferred route is the pick when its fit reads yes, alternatives are the other fitting routes by fit probability, and confidence comes from the reading outcome (task-routes/planner.ts, route-selector.ts). |
| `agent-route-planner-candidates-setup.ts` (whole file, calls into helpers above) | Applies the keyword-ladder predicates to decide setup/host-diagnostics/settings-import/settings/model-provider/personality/memory/personal-ops route candidates and their confidence | Hoisted in E.4: the routes are catalog entries (task-routes/catalog-setup.ts) chosen by `routing.task-route.pick`. |

| `agent-route-tool.ts`, `execute` (L94-98) | Exposes the keyword-ladder planner above as a model-callable `route action:"plan"` | Hoisted in E.4: `createTaskRouteTool` calls `planTaskRoute` (task-routes/tool.ts). |

| `agent-policy-explanation.ts`, `resolveToolName` (L127-159) | Exact match, then case-insensitive match, then substring-of-description search over every registered tool definition to resolve a free-text lookup target to one tool, with an "ambiguous" candidate list on multiple matches | JEV entity alignment / choice pattern |
| `agent-model-compare-types.ts`, `SYNTHESIS_THEMES` (L181-191), consumed by `agent-model-compare-judgment.ts`'s `formatComparisonSynthesis` | A six-entry regex-pattern ladder (e.g. `/concrete\|actionable\|specific.../i`) classifying a human judge's free-text `reasons`/`notes` into cross-session preference themes | JEV rerank/choice pattern classifying judgment reasoning against a fixed theme taxonomy |
| `agent-model-compare-run.ts`, `resolveRequestedModels` (L58-85) | Progressively looser string matching (exact registryKey, then `provider:model`, then modelId, then displayName, then substring) to resolve a user-typed model reference to one catalog entry | JEV entity alignment pattern |
| `agent-delegation-tool.ts` (facade; heuristic lives in the already-covered harness) | A harness-side heuristic chooses local-first vs. delegated/isolated/remote execution for a task with no acceptance-criteria judgment of the outcome | Contract-runner group/unit assignment (JEV routing pattern), per the owner ruling |
| `agent-work-plan-tool.ts`, `createAgentWorkPlanTool`/`dispatchAgentsFromWorkPlan` (whole file) | Local `WorkPlanStore` CRUD plus ad-hoc agent spawn (`agent` tool `spawn`/`batch-spawn`); "done" is whatever the dispatched agent self-reports, with no judged acceptance criteria | Contract-runner unit/group submission judged against stated acceptance criteria (JEV verification reading), per the owner ruling |
| `agent-workspace-tool.ts` (whole file) | Workspace actions execute directly behind only a boolean `confirm` gate; no judgment of whether the action's result actually satisfied the request | Contract-runner verb submission with Jev-judged unit completion, per the owner ruling |

## Test: cross-cutting miscellany

This slice covers 84 files drawn from `src/test/acp`, `src/test/agents`, `src/test/artifacts`, `src/test/automation`, `src/test/browser`, `src/test/channels`, `src/test/chaos`, `src/test/contracts`, `src/test/control-plane`, `src/test/daemon`, `src/test/deps`, `src/test/docs`, `src/test/features`, `src/test/fixtures`, `src/test/git`, `src/test/helpers`, `src/test/hooks` and `src/test/integration`, the alphabetically first half of a cross-cutting test miscellany. Since the directory name for a test file rarely names its real subject, every file was read in full and classified by what it actually imports and exercises (the SDK/engine module under test, or the local runtime/product module), not by its folder. Where a file imports from `@pellux/goodvibes-sdk/platform/*`, that subpath was matched against the intent document's engine subsystem table to find its disposition; where a file exercises this repo's own `src/runtime`, `src/agent`, `src/tools` etc., the matching product-level PORT/JEV/HOIST/DROP call in the intent document's agent-product section was used instead. Test helpers and non-`.test.ts` fixtures (spawned child-process probes, TS hook fixtures, OpenClaw import fixtures) were classified by the subject of the module or feature they support.

Counts: 84 files. PORT 75, JEV 7, HOIST 2, DROP 0.

The intent's engine table lists "discovery, mcp, plugins, acp" as PORT; nothing here is WRFC- or QEMU-specific. |

This slice covers 83 files, the alphabetically second half of a cross-cutting test miscellany
under `src/test/` in goodvibes-agent (integration, integrations, intelligence, knowledge, mcp,
media, multimodal, plugins, release-gates, scheduler, scripts, security, sessions, setup.ts,
state, ux, watchers, web-search, work-plans, workflow). None of these directory names are
themselves engine subsystems, so for every file the method was the same: read the file in full,
find what it actually imports and exercises (an SDK `platform/*` module, this repo's own
`@/runtime`, or a plain build/CI script), and give the file the disposition that real subject has
per the intent document's engine subsystem table and the owner ruling voiding the work-plan/
delegation/orchestration DROP lines. Where a subsystem is PORT overall but a specific file's own
code contains a guessed classification (a keyword/substring ladder over free text, a fixed
numeric quality threshold, a risk/trust label attached to unstructured input), that file is
marked JEV and a decision-points row is added; where a file only exercises the deterministic,
already-PORT parts of an otherwise-JEV subsystem (plain parsing, CRUD, contract-shape checks over
a JEV surface), it is marked JEV or PORT per the subsystem call below but gets no decision-points
row of its own, the same restraint `docs/inventory/webui.md` uses for its contract-tree view
files. Three files test the agent's own capability/trust/card-intake surfaces that the intent
document explicitly lists as HOIST targets into the engine; none of the 83 files touch anything
WRFC-controller-only or QEMU-sandbox-only, so this slice has zero DROP rows.

### Decision points

| Where | Guessed today | Replaced by |
|---|---|---|
| `PermissionManager`/`permissions.mode` (exercised in `integration/permission-flow.test.ts`, `integration/tool-execution.test.ts`, `security/permission-audit.test.ts`) | A three-way mode enum (prompt/allow-all/custom) plus a fixed per-tool action table (allow/prompt/deny/delegate) picked by the operator, with no graduated sense of stakes | Gate presets over a stakes table (graduated autonomy), per the engine gate row |
| `classifyDeliveryError` (`integrations/delivery.test.ts`) | A substring/HTTP-status ladder over free-text error messages ("timeout", "aborted", "ECONNREFUSED", 4xx/5xx), defaulting unknown errors to retryable | A Jev yes/no reading of retryable-vs-terminal, no keyword fallback |
| `GitHubIntegration.eventToPrompt`'s `issue_comment` handling (`integrations/github.test.ts`) | A substring check for whether a comment body mentions/addresses the bot ("@goodvibes") before generating a prompt | A Jev intent-to-handler reading (does this message address the agent) |
| Knowledge ingest acceptance and review scoring (`knowledge/graphql.test.ts`, `knowledge/knowledge-api.test.ts`, `knowledge/service.test.ts`) | Ingested sources are accepted on successful parse/fetch alone, with `review.confidence`/`trustTier` set as plain input data rather than computed | Jev gated writes and quality scoring on a specificity rubric before acceptance |
| Knowledge consolidation candidates/reports (`knowledge/graphql.test.ts`, `knowledge/service.test.ts`, light/deep `runJob` calls) | Fixed job logic classifies and groups consolidation candidates | Jev duplicate detection by entity alignment and usefulness scoring |
| MCP server `trustMode`/risk classification (`mcp/mcp-api.test.ts`, `mcp/registry.test.ts`, `release-gates/runtime-knowledge-security-gate.test.ts`'s `buildMcpAttackPathReview`) | A fixed label (`ask-on-risk`, `riskLevel: 'critical'`) attached to a server/tool call to decide isolation, quarantine, and approval | Gate's side-effect, risk-family and sandbox-advisory batteries |
| `classifyFailure` (`release-gates/operability-gate.test.ts`) | A precedence-ordered ladder over structured flags plus free-text `errorMessage` substrings ("timed out", "API error", "network failure"), defaulting to `unknown` | A Jev choice reading over the closed `FailureClass` set |
| `computeQualityScore`/`LOW_QUALITY_THRESHOLD` (`release-gates/performance-gate.test.ts`) | Compaction output quality scored by a fixed numeric threshold (0.4) to decide strategy escalation | Jev's fidelity-check pattern for compaction quality |
| Knowledge injection `ingestMode` (`release-gates/runtime-knowledge-security-gate.test.ts`'s `buildKnowledgeInjectionPrompt`, `ingestMode: 'keyword-ranked'`) | Retrieved knowledge is ranked into the prompt by a named keyword-ranking mode | Jev's rerank and existence-check pattern on retrieval |
